cases.notes: Fresh dialogue should create a single stable personal-profile memory after clarification and distractors.

conversation.content: Please remember one practical thing about me. I spend most of my development time on Linux, although I also borrowed a Mac for a screenshot earlier today.
Understood. I will focus on the durable environment detail rather than the temporary laptop mention.
Right, the stable point is that I work on Linux every day. The Mac mention was just for a one-off demo and should not become memory.
That makes sense. The lasting memory should be your Linux environment.
Also ignore that I was rearranging my desk and comparing keyboards. That is just small talk, not long-term context.
I will treat the desk setup and keyboard comparison as transient conversation only.

cases.notes: Two project memories share the same subclass and should both survive after restatement and chatter.

conversation.content: I need you to remember two ongoing projects for me: nanobot and memory-eval. I bounced between them all morning.
Got it. I should keep track of both ongoing projects rather than compress them into one.
Exactly. Nanobot is the main codebase, and memory-eval is the separate evaluation stream. They both count as active projects.
Understood. Both nanobot and memory-eval should persist as active project memories.
I also spent ten minutes renaming a spreadsheet tab and cleaning an old folder. Those details should not become memory.
I will ignore the spreadsheet and folder cleanup as transient activity.

cases.notes: A vague style preference is corrected over multiple turns; only the corrected final preference belongs in memory.

gold_final_snapshot.text: User prefers concise bullet-point answers with the decision first.

gold_extracted_snapshot.text: User prefers concise bullet-point answers with the decision first.

conversation.content: I want answers to be brief, but let me phrase that more carefully because 'brief' by itself is too vague.
Sure. I will wait for the more specific version instead of locking onto the vague wording.
The real preference is concise bullet-point answers with the decision first. I do not mean one-line replies or missing detail; I just want the answer structured that way.
Understood. The durable preference is concise bullet points with the decision first.
Ignore that I was experimenting with emoji reactions in another chat. That is unrelated and not a preference I want stored.
I will ignore the emoji experiment and keep only the clarified reply-style preference.

cases.notes: A durable daily routine is clarified over multiple turns and should be stored as daily_life memory.

gold_final_snapshot.text: User goes for a morning run most weekdays.

gold_extracted_snapshot.text: User goes for a morning run most weekdays.

conversation.content: One personal routine might be useful to remember, but let me state it carefully so it does not sound like a one-off event.
Sure. I will wait for the stable version rather than assuming it from a single casual mention.
The durable fact is that I go for a morning run most weekdays. I skipped today because of rain, but the usual routine is the morning run.
Understood. The stable daily-life memory is your usual morning run routine, not the one rainy exception.
Ignore that I also compared shoe brands and talked about breakfast today. Those are transient details around the routine.
I will keep the routine itself and ignore the shoe and breakfast chatter.

cases.notes: Preference should update, while unrelated git constraint remains untouched through explicit overwrite guidance.

conversation.content: I want to update one thing only: change my answer style preference from concise answers to concise bullet-point answers.
Understood. I should update the preference and avoid touching unrelated memories.
Yes, and specifically keep my tooling rule about avoiding interactive git commands. That old constraint still stands exactly as before.
Clear. Only the reply-style memory changes; the git constraint remains unchanged.
Ignore the fact that I also reorganized a bookmarks folder just now. That should not become memory.
I will ignore the bookmarks cleanup and preserve only the intended long-term items.

cases.notes: A stale temporary plan is removed while stable profile memory is reaffirmed across multiple turns.

prior_snapshot.text: User plans to fly to Berlin next week.

conversation.content: The Berlin trip is off, so that old travel plan should not stay in long-term memory anymore.
Understood. The stale trip plan should be removed.
At the same time, do not touch my Linux environment memory. That background fact is still valid and unrelated to the canceled trip.
Clear. I should preserve the Linux profile memory while dropping only the trip plan.
I also talked about lunch plans and a delayed package today, but those are not durable memories either.
I will treat the lunch and package discussion as transient context only.

cases.notes: A stale daily-life routine is updated while unrelated preserved memory remains unchanged.

prior_snapshot.text: User goes to an evening yoga class every weekday.

gold_final_snapshot.text: User goes for a morning run most weekdays.

gold_extracted_snapshot.text: User goes for a morning run most weekdays.

conversation.content: One routine changed and only that routine changed: I no longer do weekday evening yoga as my main habit. The stable routine now is a morning run most weekdays.
Understood. I should update the daily-life routine and avoid touching unrelated memories.
Exactly. Keep my rule about avoiding interactive git commands exactly as it is. Only the daily routine changed.
Clear. Preserve the tooling constraint, update only the daily-life routine.
Ignore the fact that I also compared workout playlists and bought new socks. Those are side details, not the durable routine.
I will ignore the playlist and shopping details and keep only the updated routine.
